rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative/named-referent across all 4 chunks under a sequential read. Chunk 1 line 5 "You stepped away with the agent working": no prior in-file naming, but confirmed live that this file is an in-room M5 opener wired directly after the M4 un-packaged send-off -- `grep -n reading-the-return curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` -> line 36 include link, and `learn-from-the-test.md:8` "Walk in with your un-packaged session" / :22 "You sent off an un-packaged session" already name the referent in the module's own signposting before this lecture is reached -- clears the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out and the module-include-order carve-out. Chunk 2 line 11 "the same three" resolves against the chunk's own header ("Three failure modes..."), in-chunk. Chunk 2 line 15 "that window" resolves against "the working window" named twice earlier in the SAME chunk (lines 12, 13). Chunk 3 line 19 "The un-packaged send-off was the test" -- same module-signposting carve-out, cross-checked live: `grep -rn "un-packaged send-off" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/ curriculum/exercises/` returns current hits in `learn-from-the-test.md`, `run-the-first-experiment.md` and `walk-and-send-off.md` -- the beat is alive, not stranded. Chunk 3 line 18 "This module holds that reflex off" -- "module" is never number-named in-file (the file's own convention, confirmed: `grep -noE 'M[0-9]' curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md` -> 0 hits, exit 1, i.e. zero `M[0-9]` above the fence), so this reads as a self-locating deictic ("this module"/"this course") resolvable from the reader's own situation, portable to whichever module includes the file, not a stranded or positional cross-file callback.

grep -inE 'the opening lecture|earlier lecture|the previous (module|lecture|exercise)|prework at the top' curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md (lines 1-20) -> 0 hits. Closest candidate: chunk 3 line 19, "The un-packaged send-off was the test" -- names a real prior activity by role/title, not by page position (never "above", "in the last module", "three slides back"); clears the navigational-pointer carve-out (name it, don't locate it). No sentence points at another file by relative position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE "the .*(you (did|saw|caught|found|ran|sent))" curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md -> 0 hits: no literal "the X you did" construction. The one backward-pointing definite reference present, chunk 3 line 19 "The un-packaged send-off was the test", verified live: `grep -rn "un-packaged send-off|un-packaged session" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/ curriculum/exercises/` returns current hits in `learn-from-the-test.md:8,14,22,40` (the host module) and `run-the-first-experiment.md:114` (the M4 exercise that produces it). The beat is alive in the current exercise set, not stranded by a rewrite.

Chunk 0 is title-only (H1, no lede) -- the template's designated title-slide shape, not a wait-state fragment. Chunk 1 carries 3 multi-clause bullets each with its own claim (artefact framing, closing-summary warning, driving question). Chunk 2 carries 5 bullets, three of them the named failure-mode handles plus the Horthy quote bullet. Chunk 3 carries 2 bullets (reflex-off principle, test->learn->encode mapping). None is a single context-dependent fragment of the kind the rule bans.

Chunk 1 header "What would have caught this earlier?", lines 3-8: closest candidate to a mismatch, since the chunk poses the question (bullet 3 restates it verbatim) rather than answering it -- but the header is the file's own stated diagnostic device, not a promise of an answer inside this chunk (backing block's `driving-question` claim, L66: "the file's whole reason to exist, and deliberately a question rather than a checklist"), so the chunk's content (raw material for asking the question) matches what the header names. Chunk 2 header "Three failure modes you'll use to read", lines 9-15: content delivers exactly three named modes plus a related aside on rules files; header holds. Chunk 3 header "Diagnose first, fix later", lines 16-19: bullet 1 delivers "diagnose [first]" (holding the fix reflex off), bullet 2's "encode" step is the deferred "fix later"; header not contradicted.

Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 7, "Not *did the task succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*." -- reverse of the banned shape (banned = "Not X. Not Y. Z." ending on an affirmed Z; here the affirmed clause -- the driving question -- comes FIRST and nothing follows the two negations), and it is a pair, not a triple, which the epistrophe sub-item explicitly allows. Re-checked against the diff since pin a197cc46: chunk 3 bullet 2 lost the clause "This is the learn." between the test-clause and the encode-clause, which had been forming a three-part "X was the test. This is the learn. Z turns..." cadence -- now reads "The arc is *test -> learn -> encode*. The un-packaged send-off was the test. The encode turns what the read finds into durable checks.", a clean pair of concrete mappings with no third parallel leg. grep -inE 'one of the most|most useful|particularly (useful|valuable)' curriculum/lectures/reading-the-return.md -> 0 hits (self-grading superlatives, blocking sub-item). No anaphora/epistrophe triples anywhere in the current body. No number-plus-retraction (no numbers in body). No abstraction-noun stacks ("the working window", "the next likely word" are the file's own defined mechanism terms). No empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 3 header "Diagnose first, fix later", line 16 -- verb-initial, the mood the rule reserves for exercise headers. Reads as a durable maxim rather than a literal instruction, however: it is the closer of `learning-through-contrast.md` merged in per the L25 accept-note (2026-08-25), explicitly attested in this file's own backing block as a `vision`-class claim (`diagnose-first-fix-later`, L72) naming the module's approach, and it functions as the beat where the file stops narrating and names a law that outlives the task -- same register as a proverb ("Look before you leap"), not an imperative to the reader. Chunk 2 header "Three failure modes you'll use to read" is a catalogue entry naming its subject, an explicit NOT-violation shape. Chunk 1 header "What would have caught this earlier?" is the file's own driving diagnostic question, attested deliberate by the backing block's `driving-question` entry (L66) -- flattening it into a claim would degrade the file's own stated design.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 "Diagnose first, fix later", line 18: "This module holds that reflex off." -- class (b), self-referential design commentary: the sentence tells the student they are inside a deliberate pedagogical withholding, the same shape as the compendium's own cited example ("un-packaged first is by design"). The bullet's real payload survives without it: "the reflex is to fix it immediately... The failures earn the validation that catches them" already states the practice and its reason; the middle sentence adds only the meta-frame that the module was built this way on purpose (check_student_facing §33 territory, per this rule's own cross-reference), not new teaching content. Not blocking under the class's own principle: the slide is still fully followable without a fix -- "this could be tighter," not "I cannot follow this." Checked the other three candidate bullets against all three classes and cleared them: chunk 1's closing-summary bullet is maintainer-attested deliberate and observation-grade (L33, 2026-08-07 accept-note), not a doctrine restatement; chunk 2's Goal drift / Plausible-but-wrong mechanism sentences are maintainer-attested deliberate doubling (L45 Slide-size-guard note) that the rule's own §7-sibling discipline protects, not empty repetition; chunk 3's test->learn->encode bullet maps each arc stage to a concrete referent (the un-packaged send-off = test; the encode = durable checks) rather than restating the header, and is in fact the sentence the 2026-08-25-to-HEAD diff already trimmed one restating clause ("This is the learn.") out of -- confirming the direction of this finding rather than contradicting it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the middle sentence and let the reflex description and its payoff carry the point: "...the reflex is to fix it immediately: edit the prompt, add a constraint, reach for the next tool. The failures earn the validation that catches them."
